## Overview

`deepImp` imputes missing values with configurable neural networks, for both
mixed-type data (`impNNet()`) and compositional data with rounded zeros
(`impNNetCoDa()`). Networks run on a native **torch** backend by default (no
Python required) or, optionally, on **keras3**. The architecture is described by
a `deepimp_arch()` object.

```{r}
library(deepImp)
arch <- deepimp_arch(hidden = c(128, 64), dropout = 0.1, activation = "relu")
arch
```

## Mixed-type imputation

The `beer` data (bundled) contains volatile-compound measurements. We introduce
missing values completely at random and impute them.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
data(beer, package = "deepImp")
set.seed(1)
b <- beer
b[cbind(sample(nrow(b), 20), sample(ncol(b), 20, replace = TRUE))] <- NA

imp <- impNNet(b, arch = deepimp_arch_small(), epochs = 100, seed = 1)
imp
completed <- getImputed(imp)
head(completed)
```

`getImputed(imp)` returns the completed data frame; `summary(imp)` reports the
imputed cells per variable and `plot(imp)` shows the convergence of the chained
imputation.

## Compositional data: rounded zeros

For compositional data, values below a detection limit ("rounded zeros") are
imputed in log-ratio coordinates and censored at the limit, following
Templ (2021). Detection limits are supplied via `dl`.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
data(expenditures, package = "robCompositions")
x <- expenditures
dl <- apply(x, 2, function(z) 0.1 * min(z[z > 0]))   # example detection limits
x[x < matrix(dl, nrow(x), ncol(x), byrow = TRUE)] <- 0

imp <- impNNetCoDa(x, dl = dl, label = 0, correction = "truncate",
                   arch = deepimp_arch_small(), epochs = 100, seed = 1)
head(getImputed(imp))
```

`correction = "truncate"` (default) sets imputed parts above the detection limit
to the limit, as in Templ (2021); `"expectation"` uses a truncated-normal mean;
`"none"` disables censoring.

## Backends and reproducibility

Select the backend per call with `backend = "torch"` (default) or
`backend = "keras"` (requires `keras3` and `keras3::install_keras()`). A `seed`
makes a run reproducible within a backend; the two backends do not produce
identical numbers.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
imp_keras <- impNNet(b, backend = "keras", arch = deepimp_arch_small(),
                     epochs = 100, seed = 1)
```

Note: with `m > 1`, `impNNet()`/`impNNetCoDa()` return several completed data
sets, but these are stochastic replicate completions, **not** statistically
valid multiple imputation.

## Reference

Templ, M. (2021). Imputation of rounded zeros for high-dimensional compositional
data using neural networks.
